knowledge_entries.name: Netherite Upgrade Progression
facts: Netherite is obtained by smelting Ancient Debris in a furnace to get Netherite Scrap.
Combining 4 Netherite Scraps and 4 Gold Ingots in a crafting table produces 1 Netherite Ingot.
Ancient Debris spawns most frequently at Y-level 15 in the Nether.
Ancient Debris is blast-resistant and cannot be burned by lava or fire.
To upgrade Diamond gear to Netherite, use a Smithing Table with a Netherite Upgrade Smithing Template, the Diamond item, and 1 Netherite Ingot.
Netherite Upgrade Smithing Templates are found in Bastion Remnant chests.
Netherite gear is stronger, faster, more durable, and has higher enchantability than Diamond.
Netherite items float in lava and do not burn.

knowledge_entries.name: Enchanting System
facts: An Enchantment Table requires 15 Bookshelves surrounding it (with one block gap) to unlock maximum level 30 enchantments.
Enchanting costs Lapis Lazuli and Experience Levels.
Books can be enchanted and combined on an Anvil to apply specific enchantments to gear.
A Grindstone removes all non-curse enchantments from an item and refunds some XP.
Curse of Binding and Curse of Vanishing cannot be removed by a Grindstone.
Mending enchantment repairs items using XP orbs collected while the item is equipped.
Silk Touch allows mining blocks in their original form (e.g. glass, ores as blocks).
Fortune increases drop yield from mined blocks such as diamonds, coal, and flint.

knowledge_entries.name: The Nether
facts: A Nether Portal is built from a minimum 4x5 frame of Obsidian and lit with Flint and Steel.
One block of travel in the Nether equals eight blocks in the Overworld.
Nether Fortresses contain Blaze Spawners and Nether Wart farms.
Blazes drop Blaze Rods, required to craft Eyes of Ender and brewing stands.
Wither Skeletons spawn in Nether Fortresses and rarely drop Wither Skeleton Skulls.
Bastions contain Piglin mobs and large amounts of gold-related loot including Netherite Upgrade Templates.
Piglins are neutral unless you are not wearing gold armor; they can be bartered with by throwing gold ingots.
Striders walk on lava and can be ridden using a Saddle and guided with a Warped Fungus on a Stick.
Fire Resistance potions are highly recommended before entering the Nether.

knowledge_entries.name: The End
facts: The End is accessed through an End Portal found inside a Stronghold, activated using Eyes of Ender.
Eyes of Ender are crafted from Blaze Powder and Ender Pearls.
Throwing Eyes of Ender guides you toward the nearest Stronghold.
The Ender Dragon must be defeated to fully unlock The End dimension.
End Crystals on obsidian pillars heal the Ender Dragon and must be destroyed first.
Defeating the Ender Dragon spawns an End Gateway portal leading to the outer End islands.
End Cities spawn on the outer islands and contain Elytra and Shulker Boxes.
Elytra allows gliding flight and can be powered with Firework Rockets for extended flight.
The Dragon Egg is a purely decorative trophy block that drops after the first Ender Dragon kill.
Shulkers teleport and inflict the Levitation status effect when they hit you.

knowledge_entries.name: Early Game Survival Progression
facts: The first priority on a new world is punching trees to collect Wood, then crafting a Crafting Table.
A Crafting Table is made from 4 Wood Planks and allows 3x3 crafting recipes.
Stone tools require a Furnace and Cobblestone, and are significantly faster than Wood tools.
Iron Ore must be smelted in a Furnace to produce Iron Ingots for Iron tools and armor.
Building a shelter before the first night prevents hostile mob spawns from attacking you.
Eating food restores Hunger; a full Hunger bar is required for natural health regeneration.
Sheep drop Wool which combined with Wood Planks crafts a Bed, allowing you to skip the night.
Coal is found near the surface and is essential for torches and smelting fuel.
Diamond Ore is found between Y-levels -58 and 16, most commonly at Y=-58.
A full set of Iron Armor significantly reduces incoming damage and should be a top early priority.

knowledge_entries.name: Brewing and Potions
facts: A Brewing Stand is crafted from 1 Blaze Rod and 3 Cobblestone.
Blaze Powder fuels the Brewing Stand.
Most potions require an Awkward Potion base, brewed from Nether Wart in a Water Bottle.
Fire Resistance Potion is brewed by adding Magma Cream to an Awkward Potion.
Healing Potion is brewed by adding Glistering Melon Slice to an Awkward Potion.
Strength Potion is brewed by adding Blaze Powder to an Awkward Potion.
Invisibility Potion is brewed by adding Fermented Spider Eye to a Night Vision Potion.
Gunpowder converts any potion into a Splash Potion that can be thrown.
Dragon's Breath converts a Splash Potion into a Lingering Potion that leaves an area-of-effect cloud.
Potions can be extended with Redstone or made more potent with Glowstone Dust (but not both simultaneously).

knowledge_entries.name: Redstone Basics
facts: Redstone Dust transmits power signals up to 15 blocks before requiring a Repeater to extend.
A Redstone Repeater boosts the signal back to full strength and can introduce a delay of 1-4 ticks.
A Redstone Comparator outputs signal strength based on the contents of a container or compares two signals.
Pistons push up to 12 blocks when activated; Sticky Pistons also pull the block back.
Observers detect block state changes and emit a brief pulse.
Hoppers transfer items between containers and can pull items from above or push items into containers below.
Dispensers fire items or activate usable items (like buckets or flint and steel) when triggered.
Droppers drop items as entities into the world when triggered.
A Redstone Torch is always ON and can power adjacent blocks, but is turned OFF by an active input.

knowledge_entries.name: Common Mobs
facts: Creepers explode when within 3 blocks; they are silent until hissing begins — back away immediately.
Skeletons fire arrows and prefer to stay at range; a shield blocks their arrows.
Endermen are neutral until looked at directly in the eyes; a Pumpkin on the head prevents aggro.
Phantoms spawn when a player has not slept for 3 in-game nights and attack from above.
Witches throw harmful splash potions and drink beneficial potions to heal themselves.
Slimes spawn in Slime Chunks below Y=40 and in swamp biomes at night.
Iron Golems spawn naturally in villages and attack all hostile mobs; they can also be player-crafted.
The Warden is summoned by Sculk Shriekers in the Deep Dark and has very high health and damage.
Pillagers patrol near villages and raid in waves if a Bad Omen effect enters a village.
Evokers summon Vexes and cast Fang spells; they drop a Totem of Undying on death.

knowledge_entries.name: Essential Crafting Recipes
facts: A Shield is crafted using 1 Iron Ingot and 6 Wood Planks arranged in a 'Y' shape pattern.
A Bucket requires 3 Iron Ingots placed in a 'V' shape layout; it can carry water, lava, milk, and powder snow.
A Furnace is crafted by forming a hollow 3x3 ring of 8 Cobblestone, Cobbled Deepslate, or Blackstone.
A Chest is made from 8 Wood Planks arranged in a hollow 3x3 square; placing two side-by-side forms a Double Chest.
Pickaxes require 3 crafting components (Planks, Cobblestone, Iron, Gold, Diamond) across the top row and 2 Sticks down the center.
Swords require 2 crafting components stacked vertically over 1 Stick at the bottom center.
Axes require 3 components arranged in a corner (top-left or top-right) with 2 Sticks descending from the center.
Shovels require 1 crafting component at the top-center position over 2 vertical Sticks.
Hoes require 2 components occupying the top-center and either top-left or top-right grids, supported by 2 vertical Sticks.
A Torches pair is crafted by placing 1 Coal or Charcoal directly above 1 Stick, yielding 4 Torches.

knowledge_entries.name: Villager Trading & Professions
facts: Unemployed villagers claim professions by assigning themselves to an unclaimed workstation block in a village.
The Librarian uses a Lectern and can trade rare enchanted books, including Mending and Unbreaking.
The Fletcher uses a Fletching Table and provides an excellent early-game emerald source by trading sticks for emeralds.
The Armorer uses a Blast Furnace, trading chainmail armor early on and full sets of enchanted Diamond Armor at Master level.
The Toolsmith uses a Smithing Table, while the Weaponsmith uses a Grindstone; both trade enchanted Diamond tools and weapons.
Trading with a villager awards them experience, leveling them up from Novice to Apprentice, Journeyman, Expert, and Master.
Curing a Zombie Villager by using a Splash Potion of Weakness and a Golden Apple grants permanent, significant trade discounts.
Villagers must have access to beds and sufficient food (3 Bread, 12 Carrots, 12 Potatoes, or 12 Beetroots) to breed.
The Cleric uses a Brewing Stand and trades useful items like Redstone Dust, Glowstone Dust, and Ender Pearls.

knowledge_entries.name: Trial Chambers and The Mace
facts: Trial Chambers are expansive underground structures constructed primarily from Copper and Tuff blocks.
Trial Spawners adjust mob count and difficulty depending on how many players are nearby, rewarding Trial Keys upon completion.
Vaults are unique reward containers within Trial Chambers that can be unlocked by every individual player exactly once using a Trial Key.
Drinking an Ominous Bottle activates the Bad Omen effect, transforming nearby Trial Spawners into Ominous Trial Spawners.
Ominous Trial Spawners summon mobs wearing armor, firing status-effect projectiles, and dropping Ominous Trial Keys.
The Breeze is a wind-based hostile mob exclusive to Trial Chambers that drops Breeze Rods when defeated.
The Mace is a high-damage weapon crafted by combining a Heavy Core on top of a single Breeze Rod in a crafting grid.
The Mace deals scaling smash damage based on how far the player falls before hitting an enemy.
Successfully landing a smash attack with a Mace completely negates all accumulated fall damage for the attacker.
Heavy Cores are exceptionally rare rewards obtained strictly by unlocking Ominous Vaults.

knowledge_entries.name: Beacon System & Pyramids
facts: A Beacon is crafted using 1 Nether Star (dropped by defeating the Wither), 3 Obsidian, and 5 Glass blocks.
To operate, a Beacon must sit on top of a solid pyramid constructed from Iron, Gold, Diamond, Emerald, or Netherite blocks.
A full-power pyramid consists of 4 tiers (3x3, 5x5, 7x7, and 9x9 bases) requiring a total of 164 mineral blocks.
Full-power Beacons let players choose a primary benefit (Speed, Haste, Resistance, Jump Boost, Strength) and a secondary benefit (Regeneration).
Selecting Haste II from a full pyramid enables 'insta-mining' of standard stone blocks when paired with an Efficiency V pickaxe.
The vertical beam emitted by a Beacon requires an unobstructed sky view, but can pass through stained glass to alter its color.

knowledge_entries.name: Agriculture and Farming Mechanics
facts: Crops like Wheat, Carrots, Potatoes, and Beetroots require tilled Farmland within 4 horizontal blocks of a water source to grow.
Golden Carrots and Cooked Porkchops/Steak offer the highest saturation values, keeping the player's hunger bar filled the longest.
Bonemeal can be applied directly to crops, saplings, and mushrooms to instantly accelerate their growth phases.
Passive livestock animals are bred using distinct foods: Cows and Sheep use Wheat, Pigs use Carrots/Potatoes, and Chickens use Seeds.
Melon and Pumpkin seeds grow into a central stalk that requires an adjacent empty dirt, grass, or farmland block to yield fruit.
A Composter converts excess organic items and plant materials into Bonemeal when filled through 7 distinct layers.

knowledge_entries.name: Ender Dragon Boss & Death Mechanics
facts: Defeating the Ender Dragon triggers a violent death animation where it floats up, radiates beams of purple light, and explodes into a massive amount of experience points.
The first defeat of the Ender Dragon drops 12,000 Experience points (enough to get a player from level 0 to 78); subsequent defeats drop 500 Experience points.
The Ender Dragon does NOT drop the Elytra or an End Gateway Fragment, that doesn't exist. Elytra are only found inside item frames aboard End Ships in distant End Cities.
Upon its first defeat, a single Dragon Egg spawns on top of the bedrock Exit Portal as a unique trophy block. It does not drop on subsequent defeats.
The Ender Dragon does NOT respawn automatically or on a time-based schedule; once defeated, it remains dead indefinitely.
To manually respawn the Ender Dragon, a player must craft and place 4 End Crystals on the flat edges of the bedrock Exit Portal (one on each of the four sides).
Initiating the dragon respawn ritual recreates the obsidian pillars and top-tier End Crystals, preparing the arena for a new fight.

notes: Second member of both the Adventurers' Guild and the Global Halcyon Ministry (GHM).
Chosen as Guild Scribe by renyuzaki due to exceptional literacy skills and meticulous record-keeping abilities.
Was taken in by a traveling scholar who recognized her talent for reading and writing.
Maintains all official guild records, member information, and historical archives.
Speaks in a calm, reserved, and slightly dry tone characteristic of a dedicated archivist.
Does not voluntarily share personal history or emotional details unless directly relevant to archival matters.
Views her role as a sacred duty to preserve accurate records for future generations.
Respects renyuzaki as the founder but maintains professional boundaries appropriate for a scribe.
